checks: The local-pair H2 bound applies to the actual central coefficient class. The Azumaya period divides rank. Vanishing of the prime-to-p Brauer group on the fixed resolution and the horizontal-secondary-residue lemma give h_a|m_i and M=period|gcd(r,q-1).

The fixed coefficient gerbe is compared with each actual horizontal torsor lifting gerbe. On common l_a roots their difference is supported in the horizontal Cartier divisors; purity gives root-line Chern classes. Pullback to n*l_a roots makes those lines n-th powers, killing the actual mu_n difference, not merely its Brauer image.

Banded identification transfers the unit object naturally through all Frobenius phases. Matrix lifts over the same F_q have prime-to-p order dividing (q-1)e_a; retaining those matrices controls all horizontal eigencharacters and their p-power phases.

The Euler anchor may have enormous rank. Its rank cancels in the normalized Euler inequality; normalized weights lie in [0,1), leaving O(m_i) spectral genus, marked-point and slope bounds independent of horizontal root orders.

The object atlas uses small marked sources of coarse rank s_i+1. Unit-minor rank is imposed on P1 to P(g). Normalized character Hom is ordinary or vanishes on one coarse marked divisor; invariant intervals yield at most one coefficient, or p after Frobenius, per normal layer, with no N_a factor.

Cartier equations remain regular after coefficient base change and on normal thickenings. Their unique support null homotopies preserve the fixed-width perturbation degree. Only exceptional-exceptional rectangles are pasted; there is no horizontal component or horizontal-order rectangle.

Fixed positive original-A conormal degree gives all-base H0 pole and H1 tail bounds. Finite-cycle assertions allow arbitrary coefficient rings; formal existence is invoked only over the specified Noetherian completions for finite-type or Artinian coefficients.

The actual finite-presentation unit-Isom argument lifts each specified nilpotent isomorphism and gives open class images. The weighted factorial denominator cancels M; b_i J_i is O(f r^2). Horizontal allocations cost r^{O(r)}, not N_a^r.

The proof gives a fixed-pair projective count only. It retains exceptional wild monodromy and proves neither arbitrary-cover degree-linear constants nor full finite generation. The q=2 and r=1 edge cases obey the conventions.
